title: The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS) Stock Price Target Cut by UBS Group - MarketBeat
content:
The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS - Get Free Report) had its target price cut by research analysts at UBS Group  from $1,150.00 to $1,010.00 in a research report issued on Monday, Benzinga reports. The firm presently has a "neutral" rating on the investment management company's stock. UBS Group's price target points to a potential upside of 13.04% from the stock's current price. A number of other analysts also recently issued reports on GS. Oppenheimer downgraded shares of The Goldman Sachs Group from a "market perform" rating to an "underperform" rating in a report on Tuesday, June 30th. Bank of America upped their price objective on shares of The Goldman Sachs Group from $1,150.00 to $1,300.00 and gave the stock a "buy" rating in a research report on Thursday, July 16th. Barclays lifted their price target on The Goldman Sachs Group from $1,048.00 to $1,245.00 and gave the company an "overweight" rating in a research note on Wednesday, July 15th. Evercore reiterated an "outperform" rating on shares of The Goldman Sachs Group in a research report on Monday, July 6th. Finally, Citigroup cut their price objective on The Goldman Sachs Group from $1,200.00 to $1,050.00 and set a "neutral" rating for the company in a research report on Wednesday, September 23rd. Ten research analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating, twelve have given a Hold rating and one  has issued  a Sell rating to the company's stock. Based on data from MarketBeat.com, the stock currently has an average rating of "Hold" and a consensus target price of $1,066.60. The Goldman Sachs Group stock traded down $9.04 during midday trading on Monday, reaching $893.52. The company's stock had a trading volume of 1,896,422 shares, compared to its average volume of 2,203,667. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 3.17, a current ratio of 0.63 and a quick ratio of 0.63. The stock has a market capitalization of $260.17 billion, a P/E ratio of 13.79, a PEG ratio of 0.93 and a beta of 1.29. The stock's 50-day simple moving average is $1,003.32 and its 200-day simple moving average is $985.60. The Goldman Sachs Group has a 52-week low of $740.01 and a 52-week high of $1,153.99. The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS - Get Free Report) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, July 14th. The investment management company reported $20.98 earnings per share for the quarter, beating analysts' consensus estimates of $14.47 by $6.51. The Goldman Sachs Group had a net margin of 15.53% and a return on equity of 19.16%. The firm had revenue of $20.34 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $16.22 billion. During the same period in the previous year, the company earned $10.91 earnings per share. The business's quarterly revenue was up 39.4% compared to the same quarter last year.  On average, sell-side analysts expect that  The Goldman Sachs Group will post 68.4 EPS for the current year. Several hedge funds have recently modified their holdings of the stock. BlackRock Inc. purchased a new position in shares of The Goldman Sachs Group during the second quarter worth approximately $24,172,123,000.  State Street Corp boosted its stake in The Goldman Sachs Group by 2.1% during the 4th quarter. State Street Corp now owns 19,564,783 shares of the investment management company's stock worth $17,197,444,000 after purchasing an additional 394,198 shares during the period.  Bank of America Corp DE acquired a new stake in The Goldman Sachs Group during the 2nd quarter worth $6,756,772,000.  Orange County Employees Retirement System purchased a new position in The Goldman Sachs Group during the 2nd quarter worth $69,537,544,000.  Finally, Corient Private Wealth LLC grew its position in The Goldman Sachs Group by 1,657.7% during the 4th quarter. Corient Private Wealth LLC now owns 2,596,487 shares of the investment management company's stock worth $2,282,312,000 after purchasing an additional 2,448,767 shares during the last quarter. 71.21% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors and hedge funds. title: GS Entec to supply 37 monopiles for Taean wind project - Ocean Energy Resources
content: GLOBAL NEWS SERVICE FOR THE FOSSIL AND RENEWABLE ENERGY COMMUNITIES GS Entec, based in Ulsan South Korea, will supply 37 monopiles for the 504-megawatt Taean offshore wind farm off the coast of Taean, South Chungcheong Province. Under a contract signed Wednesday at Taean Wind Power’s Seoul headquarters, GS Entec will begin production in July 2027 and complete deliveries by the end of August 2028. The Taean offshore wind project is being jointly developed by Singapore-based renewable energy developer Vena Energy, Danish infrastructure investor Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Korea Western Power. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2028 and finish in 2030. Once completed, the farm is expected to power about 300,000 households for a year. GS Entec entered the monopile business in 2022 through a strategic technology partnership with Dutch company Sif. It supplied all 64 monopiles for the Yeonggwang Nakwol offshore wind project in 2023 and has since secured the Taean project. The company is one of the few in South Korea with experience mass-producing and delivering large monopiles from a single domestic plant. The firm sits near the front of the roster of major financial institutions whose quarterly updates arrive in the coming sessions, placing its trading desks, advisory franchise and asset gathering operations squarely in the frame for market watchers tracking the financial sector. Its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange, where the company is a constituent of the NYSE Composite. The attention stems from timing and backdrop. The approach of the quarterly reporting window for the biggest lenders and dealers tends to lift scrutiny of every name in the group, and Goldman Sachs is frequently among the earliest to publish. Layered on top is a shifting macro picture. A weaker than expected September payrolls reading has prompted market participants to recalibrate how quickly the central bank might adjust rates, and that recalibration flows directly through the earnings mathematics of banks, dealers and advisory houses. Firms with large trading operations tend to see swings in activity when the rate narrative moves, and Goldman Sachs carries one of the most prominent franchises of that kind. The broader tone across the financial sector has been cautious in recent weeks, with several large names drifting lower as the market absorbed signals that the central bank may be slower to ease than some had assumed earlier in the year. Against that cautious backdrop, the firm's standing as a bellwether for Wall Street trading and dealmaking makes its upcoming disclosures a reference point for how the sector as a whole is navigating the environment. Goldman Sachs operates one of the most recognized franchises in global finance, spanning markets trading, advisory work on mergers and capital raising, financing, and a growing base of fee-generating asset and wealth activities. The markets business, which covers trading across equities and bonds, currencies and commodities, has long been a core engine, and its results tend to move with the level of client activity and volatility across global markets. When trading conditions are active, that unit can contribute meaningfully to the top line; when conditions quiet, the contribution tends to soften. Alongside trading sits the advisory and underwriting arm, where the firm counsels corporations on transactions and helps bring debt and equity offerings to market. This part of the business is closely tied to the broader deal environment, which itself depends on financing conditions, corporate confidence and the willingness of boards to pursue transformational transactions. A steadier rate narrative can help that pipeline, while uncertainty can slow it. The firm has also continued to build out fee-based asset and wealth operations, a deliberate effort to lean on more durable, recurring revenue streams that are less sensitive to the quarter-to-quarter swings of trading. One of the themes framing the session is the state of capital-markets activity. Underwriting of new share sales and debt issuance, together with advisory mandates on mergers, forms a central pillar of the Goldman Sachs business model, and the health of that pipeline is often read as a gauge of corporate appetite for expansion and financing. A calmer rate environment generally encourages issuers to come to market and emboldens boards to pursue deals, while abrupt moves in borrowing costs can push companies to wait. Market observers have watched for signs that the recent recalibration of rate expectations might either unlock or delay transactions, and the firm's commentary on its pipeline tends to carry weight across the sector. Trading revenue remains the other side of the capital-markets story. Periods of heightened volatility, driven by data surprises such as the recent labor reading, can lift client activity as institutions reposition. The firm's ability to intermediate large flows across asset classes is a defining feature of its model, and the balance between active trading conditions and the steadier contribution from fees is a recurring point of discussion when the company updates the market. Beyond the traditional franchise, Goldman Sachs has continued to extend its presence in digital-settlement infrastructure. Recent coverage highlighted the firm's involvement in building settlement rails tied to a very large Treasury fund, part of a broader industry effort to modernize how cash and securities move between counterparties. Work of this kind reflects a longer arc across the sector, in which established institutions apply new technology to the plumbing of financial markets, aiming to reduce friction, speed up settlement and open new fee streams. These initiatives tend to unfold over extended periods rather than all at once, and they form part of how large dealers describe their efforts to stay at the center of market structure as it evolves. Another thread running through recent commentary concerns the firm's move into a succession phase at the top of the house, even as operating results have remained firm. Transitions of senior management at large institutions draw close attention because they can affect how a firm sets strategy, retains senior talent and communicates with the market. Observers have noted the balance the firm appears to be striking between continuity in its operating performance and the planning that accompanies a change at the most senior level. How that balance is managed is one of the softer, less quantifiable factors that market watchers weigh alongside the harder numbers. The macro environment sits at the heart of the session's narrative. The softer September jobs reading pushed market participants to rethink how swiftly the central bank might move on rates, and that question matters for every corner of the financial sector. For a firm with heavy exposure to trading and dealmaking, the rate narrative shapes client behavior, financing conditions and the pace at which transactions come to market. For lenders more broadly, the same narrative influences the spread between what they earn on assets and what they pay on deposits. The interplay between a changing rate path and the readiness of the broader financial group to report makes the current stretch an especially closely watched one. Readers following the wider group can review the broader set of financial stocks to see how banks, dealers and diversified financial names are navigating the same shifting rate narrative and the approach of earnings season. Goldman Sachs operates in a crowded field of large universal banks and focused dealers, each competing for trading flow, advisory mandates and asset gathering. Rivals range from diversified lenders with sprawling consumer and commercial arms to peers more concentrated in markets and wealth. The competitive dynamic means that relative performance, not just absolute results, tends to drive the conversation when the group reports. A strong trading quarter at one house invites questions about whether peers captured similar flow, while a soft advisory stretch at one name raises the same question across the sector. This relative framing is part of why the earliest reports in the season can set the tone for those that follow. Recent developments around the firm have centered on the combination of steady operating performance, the move into a succession phase and the continued build-out of fee-based and infrastructure efforts. Operationally, the firm has emphasized its push toward more durable revenue streams in asset and wealth activities, an effort designed to temper the swings that come with a trading-heavy model. At the same time, the markets franchise remains a defining feature, and its contribution rises and falls with the activity of global clients. The blend of a cyclical trading engine and a steadier fee base is central to how the company describes its operating focus. The firm has also continued to manage capital carefully, a recurring theme for large institutions operating under evolving supervisory standards. The central bank recently finalized changes to its annual stress testing of large banks, aiming to make those exams more transparent and less volatile. Changes of that kind ripple across the sector because they influence how much capital the biggest institutions are expected to carry and how they plan their distributions and balance-sheet activity. For a firm the size of Goldman Sachs, the evolution of the supervisory framework is a standing feature of the operating environment. Several challenges frame the environment for the firm and its peers. A rate path that stays higher for longer can weigh on deal activity and financing, while abrupt swings can disrupt trading desks even as they create pockets of client activity. Competition for advisory mandates and trading flow remains intense, and fee pressure across asset management is a persistent feature of the landscape. Technology spending, cyber resilience and the modernization of market plumbing all require sustained commitment of resources. And the evolving supervisory framework adds a layer of planning that large institutions must navigate continuously. None of these factors is new, but their interaction in the current environment keeps the sector under close watch. The market environment heading into the reporting window has been defined by the tug between resilient equity benchmarks and a repricing of rate expectations. Technology and artificial-intelligence names have carried much of the broader rally, with the Nasdaq trading near record territory, while financial names have been more mixed as the rate narrative shifted. For a dealer like Goldman Sachs, that split environment tends to generate uneven activity across desks. Equity trading can stay busy when benchmarks are active, while the appetite to issue new debt or pursue acquisitions can hinge on how settled borrowing costs appear. The firm's ability to flex across these conditions, leaning on one engine when another quiets, is a recurring theme in how its model is described. Client activity is the connective thread. Institutional clients reposition portfolios when data surprises arrive, corporate clients weigh financing and transactions against the cost of capital, and wealthy households adjust how their assets are deployed. Each of these behaviors flows through a different part of the franchise, and the balance among them in any given stretch shapes the composition of revenue. The recent labor reading, by prompting a rethink of the rate path, is precisely the kind of signal that ripples through all three channels at once, which is part of why the firm drew attention as the data landed. Across the broader sector, several longer-running trends continue to shape how large dealers position themselves. The push toward more durable, fee-based revenue has been a common strategic response to the cyclicality of trading, and Goldman Sachs has leaned into asset and wealth gathering as part of that arc. The modernization of market infrastructure, including the digital-settlement work tied to a very large Treasury fund, reflects another trend in which established institutions apply technology to the plumbing of finance. And the steady evolution of the supervisory framework, including the recently finalized stress-testing changes, continues to influence how firms plan capital and balance-sheet activity. Positioning against these trends, rather than any single quarter's numbers, is often how the firm frames its longer strategic direction. The firm's scale and breadth are central to that positioning. A franchise that spans trading, advisory, financing, asset gathering and market infrastructure can draw on multiple revenue streams as conditions shift, and that diversity is a defining feature of how the company presents itself to the market. The blend of a cyclical markets engine with steadier fee-based activity is designed to let the firm navigate a range of environments, and the current stretch, with its mix of resilient equities and a repriced rate path, is a live test of that design. Because Goldman Sachs is so often read as a proxy for the health of Wall Street trading and dealmaking, its standing today carries relevance well beyond its own franchise. The firm belongs to the S&P 500, and its disclosures are frequently used as an early read on how the financial sector is weathering the macro backdrop. As the large-bank reporting calendar approaches and the rate narrative continues to shift, the firm sits at the intersection of several of the themes that define the current market environment, from the pace of central-bank adjustment to the appetite for corporate transactions and the steady modernization of market infrastructure. Taken together, the session places Goldman Sachs at the center of a sector-wide conversation about how banks and dealers are positioned as conditions evolve. The combination of an approaching reporting window, a shifting rate path, continued work on digital settlement and a carefully managed transition at the top of the house gives market watchers a broad set of threads to follow in the days ahead. title: With 17 years in education, a teacher reflects on what keeps his motivated| The New Times - The New Times
content: Helping people learn, developing young people and contributing to the community are what inspired Noel Barakamfitiye to become a teacher. ALSO READ: World Teachers’ Day: ICT Minister urges teachers to drive technology use in education That motivation has kept him in the classroom for 17 years, during which he has taught at three schools. As the world marks World Teachers’ Day on Monday, October 5, Barakamfitiye said he was overjoyed to have been part of Rwanda's education sector. He is now teaching at Kinama Primary School in Ruhango District, having previously taught at G.S. Janja in Gisagara District and G.S. Nyarugenge in Ruhango District. At Kinama Primary School, Barakamfitiye teaches Social Studies and Religious Education, Science and Elementary Technology, and Kinyarwanda. "I was inspired to become a teacher because I have always had a passion for helping others learn, developing young people, and contributing to the development of my community,” he said. He said education is one of the strongest ways to transform individuals and society, which is why he has remained committed to teaching despite the challenges that come with the profession. His 17 years in teaching have also given him the opportunity to see how the education system has evolved. One of the biggest changes, he says, has been the move from teacher-centred teaching to learner-centred learning. "Over the years, I have seen teaching become more learner-centred, with greater use of interactive teaching methods, ICT, continuous assessment, inclusive education, and competency-based learning,” he said. The changes have required teachers to use different teaching methods and resources to respond to learners with different abilities and needs. "Some of the challenges we face include large classes, limited teaching and learning resources, differences in learners’ abilities, workload, and the need to continuously adapt to new educational approaches and technologies,” he said. Barakamfitiye noted that teachers can deal with some of these difficulties through collaboration, professional development, creativity and effective classroom management, as well as working closely with parents and school administrators. What makes the work worthwhile for him is seeing learners understand what they are taught, learn new concepts, improve their performance and gain confidence. The educator finds it rewarding when former learners become responsible and successful people in society and remember the contribution their teachers made to their lives. Although teaching has not always been easy, Barakamfitiye said he has remained in the profession because he believes in its purpose. He continues to find meaning in helping learners develop academically, socially and morally. He also continues to look for ways to improve himself and become a better teacher. Barakamfitiye wants his learners to remember him as a dedicated, supportive, fair and inspiring teacher who believed in their potential. He also wants them to remember the values, discipline, confidence and positive attitude he encouraged them to develop, beyond what they learnt in the classroom.

title: Number game: Ex-DGP-turned-councillor's resignation move puts BJP on a sticky wicket in T'puram Corporation - thesouthfirst.com
content: Published Oct 04, 2026 | 12:00 PM ⚊ Updated Oct 04, 2026 | 12:01 PM R Sreelekha flanked by Mayor VV Rajesh and Deputy Mayor Asha Nath GS Synopsis: The BJP’s historic capture of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation is suddenly on shaky ground as party councillor and former DGP R Sreelekha moves to quit, putting its wafer-thin majority at risk. With the party’s one-seat majority hanging by a thread, Sreelekha makes her move, and the BJP counts its pieces. In December 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had called the BJP’s capture of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation a “watershed moment” in Keralam politics. Ten months later, that watershed victory is facing a serious test — and the trouble is from within. R. Sreelekha, the former DGP who was brought into the BJP with considerable political expectations and projected as one of its most recognisable faces in the capital, has announced her resignation as a councillor. If she stands firm on quitting, her exit comes at a particularly awkward moment for the BJP, which governs the 101-member Corporation with a one-seat cushion. Her resignation threat has once again exposed just how fragile the arithmetic behind the BJP’s historic victory remains. The party has 50 councillors and depends on independent Pattoor Radhakrishnan to reach the 51-member mark needed to retain control. With Sreelekha’s resignation, the BJP’s tally could fall to 49, leaving the NDA camp with 50 members. That makes the Sasthamangalam ward more than just another vacancy. A by-election there could determine whether the BJP can hold on to the Corporation it fought for decades to capture. For the BJP, the political irony is hard to miss. Sreelekha was inducted into the party in October 2024, elevated as a state vice-president. There was even an expectation that she could emerge as the party’s mayoral face after winning Sasthamangalam. Instead, VV Rajesh took the mayor’s post, while Asha Nath GS became the Deputy Mayor, leaving Sreelekha as just another councillor in the council she had been expected to lead. Her resignation announcement, therefore, comes less than a year after the BJP celebrated its biggest municipal breakthrough in Keralam. What began as the rise of a high-profile recruit now threatens to become an internal test of the party’s hold over the capital corporation. The question now is not merely why Sreelekha walked out. It is whether the BJP can absorb her exit, if it indeed happens, without allowing the narrow arithmetic that brought it to power in Thiruvananthapuram to unravel. Also Read: BJP’s civic majority in Thiruvananthapuram jolted as Sreelekha submits resignation to Mayor Sreelekha may have announced her resignation, but technically she continues to hold office, with the resignation yet to be submitted in the manner prescribed under the Kerala Municipality Act 1994. Sreelekha’s WhatsApp message announcing her resignation Sreelekha announced in a WhatsApp group formed for the Sasthamangalam ward that she had decided to resign for “personal reasons” and had handed over her resignation letter to Mayor Rajesh on 30 September. She said a copy would be submitted to the District Collector on 5 October. However, the Mayor and Corporation officials maintained that no formal resignation had reached the Corporation Secretary, the competent authority under the law to receive a councillor’s resignation. Rajesh sought to play down the development, saying Sreelekha had handed him a letter detailing certain personal difficulties. He stopped short of confirming that it was a resignation letter, pointing out that a councillor has to submit the resignation to the Corporation Secretary. Corporation Secretary J Muhammed Shafi also said no such communication had been received. Under Section 40 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, a councillor has to tender the resignation to the Secretary in the prescribed form. The resignation takes effect from the date the Secretary receives it, following which the fact has to be reported to the council and the State Election Commission. A Corporation official said Sreelekha had “announced” her resignation, but had not initiated the formal process. “The councillor may submit the resignation directly to the Secretary or send it by registered post, with the prescribed attestation where required. The Secretary has to acknowledge its receipt. None of that has happened in this case,” the official said. The BJP leadership, meanwhile, is understood to be in touch with Sreelekha in an effort to address her grievances. Party sources said the fact that the letter was handed over to the Mayor and not the Corporation Secretary had left room for discussions and efforts to persuade her to reconsider. Rajesh said the party was examining the concerns raised by Sreelekha and trying to find a way forward. “On the basis of the letter I got and the information shared with me, I’m trying to take things forward smoothly and address them in the way possible,” he said. For now, therefore, Sreelekha has announced her resignation, but has not formally resigned from the Corporation. Also Read: BJP councilor R Sreelekha opts out of PM-hosted Delhi visit The BJP’s historic capture of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation could soon enter a more uncertain phase, with Sreelekha’s resignation threatening to strip the ruling NDA of its wafer-thin majority. Sreelekha’s decision to quit as councillor from Sasthamangalam has changed the arithmetic of the 101-member council. If the resignation is formally moved, the BJP’s strength will come down to 49. With the support of independent councillor Pattoor Radhakrishnan, who represents Kannammoola, the NDA will have 50 members — one short of the majority mark. That leaves the BJP with a difficult stretch ahead. The party’s biggest gain in the 2025 local-body elections was winning 50 of the corporation’s 101 wards, emerging as the single largest party. But 50 was not enough to form the council on its own. Radhakrishnan’s decision to support the BJP-led NDA provided the crucial 51st vote and paved the way for the BJP to take control of the corporation for the first time. Sreelekha’s exit threatens to undo that arithmetic. For the moment, the BJP’s immediate task is to prevent the resignation from becoming final. If she remains firm, the party will have to keep the council functioning without a majority and, at the same time, prepare for the Sasthamangalam by-election. That election could become the BJP’s most important political battle in the corporation. A BJP victory would restore its strength to 50 and, with the independent’s support, take the NDA back to the 51 needed for a majority. A defeat, on the other hand, could prolong the uncertainty and give the opposition an opening to test the stability of the Rajesh-led administration. The BJP is already dealing with another vacancy-like situation. Its councillor from Vazhottukonam, R Sugathan, is in jail in connection with a case under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA). His absence has complicated the ruling front’s position in council proceedings. He has been granted six months’ leave to avoid disqualification arising from prolonged absence from council meetings. The opposition had already tested the waters earlier this year. The UDF had planned to move a no-confidence motion against the BJP-led council in June. But with only 20 councillors, it needed the LDF’s support to take the move forward. The LDF, which has 29 members, did not agree to back the initiative, forcing the UDF to drop the plan. Sreelekha’s resignation now brings the question back into focus. The LDF and UDF together have 49 councillors — exactly the strength the BJP would have after Sreelekha’s resignation. Whether that arithmetic can translate into a change of administration, however, will depend entirely on whether the two fronts are willing to work together. After the 2025 election, both the LDF and UDF chose to remain in opposition rather than join hands to prevent the BJP from taking control. Their positions have remained sharply divided on several political issues, and the LDF’s refusal to support the UDF’s earlier no-confidence initiative showed the difficulty of stitching together an anti-BJP arrangement at the corporation level. The resignation could nevertheless force both fronts to reconsider their approach. A no-confidence motion, if brought, would require the prescribed number of councillors to move it, while its success would depend on the numbers at the council. With the NDA reduced to 50, the BJP can no longer rely on the comfortable arithmetic it had at the beginning of its term. The independent councillor’s position could also assume greater significance. For the BJP, therefore, the immediate strategy is likely to be two-fold: retain the support that keeps the administration afloat and fight the Sasthamangalam by-election with the aim of restoring the lost seat. For the LDF and UDF, the dilemma is different. They now have an opportunity to challenge the BJP’s hold, but doing so would require an understanding between two fronts that have so far remained unwilling to share the same political platform in the corporation. The numbers have changed. Whether the political equations change with them remains the bigger question. Also Read: BJP’s R Sreelekha criticises party for backing out of its promise The BJP was well aware of Sreelekha’s displeasure, but it apparently did not see this move coming. The immediate challenge before the leadership is to prevent an internal disagreement from turning into a larger political embarrassment. Sreelekha had entered the Corporation election with the expectation that a BJP victory would put her in contention for the Mayor’s post. The party, however, settled on Rajesh for the position after emerging as the single largest bloc by a narrow margin. The decision did not go down well with Sreelekha, who made her dissatisfaction known within the party as well as in public. The leadership subsequently appeared to have explored the possibility of accommodating her with a position at the national level. A berth in the National Commission for Women was understood to be among the possibilities discussed. The recent appointment of Nivedita Subramanian, who had contested the Guruvayur Assembly constituency in 2016, to the National Commission for Women has added another layer to the episode. The party is now scrambling to contain the fallout. State BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar is expected to hold a direct discussion with Sreelekha in an effort to persuade her to withdraw the resignation. The differences themselves were hardly a secret within the BJP. What appears to have caught the leadership off guard was Sreelekha’s decision to take the dispute out of the party forum and announce an exit. For the BJP, it is an awkward move on a political chessboard where every piece matters. What began as a disagreement over the Mayor’s chair has now left the party having to work out its next move in the Corporation. content: Young Korean women are embracing a grown woman look, a more sophisticated and understated fashion trend, as brands shift fall and winter collections away from Y2K-style boldness. The aesthetic is also reviving interest in 2000s K-drama wardrobes from Coffee Prince, My Lovely Sam Soon and High Kick Through the Roof. Sales data and brand moves suggest the trend is already spreading beyond social media. GS Shop, the home-shopping unit of GS Retail, unveils knitwear and jackets made with 100 percent wool from its fashion brand So Natural on Sept. 23. For the fall and winter season, the brand focuses on premium materials and natural silhouettes. Courtesy of GS Shop After years of playful, edgy Y2K fashion dominating wardrobes, young Korean women are turning toward something decidedly more grown-up. The so-called "grown woman look," a Korean fashion trend centered on sophisticated, understated femininity, is gaining traction among women in their 20s and 30s. Fashion brands are responding with fall and winter collections built around polished silhouettes, richer colors and restrained styling. According to the fashion industry, the trend marks a shift away from the bold, youthful aesthetic associated with the Y2K revival. Instead, consumers are gravitating toward looks that appear effortless yet refined, with a relaxed and restrained mood. Deep colors, subtle femininity and clean silhouettes are among the defining elements. Female characters from TV dramas that aired about 20 years ago appear in Instagram search results for the Korean term "grown woman." Screenshot from Instagram The trend has even revived interest in the wardrobes of female characters from Korean TV shows that aired nearly two decades ago. On social media and in online communities, fashions worn by Han Yoo-joo, played by Chae Jung-an in the 2007 drama "Coffee Prince;" Yoo Hee-jin, played by Jung Ryeo-won in the 2005 series "My Lovely Sam Soon;" and Yoo In-na's character in the 2009 sitcom "High Kick Through the Roof" are being rediscovered as inspiration. Sales data suggest the trend is moving beyond online buzz. W Concept, an online fashion platform operated by Shinsegae Group, found that transactions for fall clothing increased more than 30 percent from Aug. 23 to 28 compared with Aug. 18 to 22. Knitwear sales jumped 85 percent, followed by mid-heeled shoes at 40 percent, tote bags at 35 percent and outerwear at 20 percent — all categories closely associated with the grown woman look. Red, burgundy and plum have also emerged as popular accent colors. LeMouton's Let's Mary Jane sneakers, launched in October last year, reached cumulative sales of 100,000 pairs within a year. Courtesy of LeMouton Casual footwear brand LeMouton has joined the trend with Mary Jane-style sneakers. Characterized by a rounded toe and a strap across the top of the foot, Mary Janes have become a natural fit for consumers seeking a feminine look without excessive embellishment. Sales of LeMouton's Mary Jane lineup reached 11 billion won ($7.8 million) through August, up 110 percent from the same period last year. GS Shop, the home-shopping business operated by GS Retail, is also targeting demand for the grown woman aesthetic. Its fashion label So Natural has chosen "soft minimalism" as its fall and winter concept, emphasizing luxurious textures including cashmere, wool and camel hair. "This fall, fashion that highlights the appeal of the material and silhouette itself rather than elaborate decoration is drawing attention, and products using cashmere and wool are proving popular," a GS Shop official said. Women's contemporary fashion brand Instantfunk reinterprets its signature aesthetic through a contemporary lens for its fall and winter collection under the concept "NEXT CHAPTER." Courtesy of Instantfunk Vintage-inspired casual brands are also embracing the shift. Women's contemporary fashion brand Instantfunk is using familiar pieces such as denim and knitwear in its fall and winter collection, pairing them with belts and accessories for a more polished aesthetic. "While maintaining the brand's existing identity, we added voluminous silhouettes, contrasting materials and accessory accents in line with the popularity of the grown woman look," an Instantfunk official said. "We are proposing a more refined and expanded style." The growing appeal of the aesthetic reflects a broader change in fashion tastes among younger Korean consumers: After seasons of crop tops, playful nostalgia and Y2K experimentation, understated sophistication is having its moment. title: McAleer: “Choosing the Battles” Gave AutoTechnic GS Title - Sportscar365
content: Stevan McAleer on taking measured approach to Pilot Challenge GS title… Stevan McAleer credited the mindset of “choosing the battles” that allowed he and Austin Krainz to secure the IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS title at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta. McAleer and Krainz drove their No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW M4 GT4 EVO to a third place finish in Friday’s Fox Factory 120, which helped BMW earn its eighth manufacturers’ championship in series competition. McAleer took control of the points lead for good after a multi-car battle following the second round of pitstops. He said the mindset of thinking big picture and knowing the points scenario before he took over driving duties from Krainz paid dividends in the second half of the race. “I know I’ve already worked out the points [of] where I need to be in what position I need to be in,” he told Sportscar365. “I’m just choosing the battles and making sure that you know we don’t go off the race track for no reason. “Just before I got in, they showed me that we were all tied on points at 2400 apiece. That’s not good because the 95 car had had a win under the belt, so they would have taken it. “The mindset is really to try and do everything we’ve done all season. Don’t mess up the pit stop, nice driver change, which we did, and a really good out and in lap. “Again, I don’t think I had a strong in-lap on the first stop, but I really nailed the second one. The racing changes so much.” McAleer battled the No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW and the No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4 both on-track and for the title. Recalling the final hour battle, McAleer said he needed balance between execution and aggressiveness. “I think again a lot of faster cars out there, but just execution and a lot of my moves were aggressive today,” he said. “But I had to force the issue to try and get by, and a couple of cars made some side to side contact, but much racing. “The race was a lot of fun. We knew what we had to do. “When you get to this stage in the championship, there’s cars that I’ll race and there’s cars that I will not race. We had to race the No. 95 and the No. 13. “We knew that the 44 car [Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4] was going to be as fast as can be, and it was to get as close to that car as we could, so the team executed perfectly. “Aside from that, a special moment for Austin and Roland [Krainz]. I could see them crying on the wall there, so it was a special moment.” McAleer won his second Pilot Challenge title after taking the 2015 championship with CJ Wilson Racing in a Mazda MX-5 in the now-defunct ST class. He said being on both slides of a title fight in the series helped him focus in the final stint. “I just put my head down and hit my marks,” said McAleer. “I’ve been in this position before, both as a winner and a loser. “We had a mechanical failure in 2016 that took another championship. Those last 20 minutes of the race, you can hear every nut and bolt creak on that car. “I honestly thought we would have would have been quite a ways off to some of the other manufacturers, but we had pace. “We’re real quick in the corners, good in breaking. We lacked a little bit in straight line speed, but we could make the rest of that up in the corners, so it was a good day.” Jack Rachinsky is a contributor to Sportscar365.com. He is currently a fourth-year broadcast journalism student at Penn State University working as a writer, broadcaster and sports director for CommRadio, the school's student-run Internet radio station. title: RU Shibir cancelled Rucsu GS Ammar's 'Sathi' membership last year, expelled over allegations of post trading - The Business Standard
content: Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar was a "Sathi" of Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir and had his status cancelled last year after failing to adequately respond to allegations including financial irregularities and the trading of positions in the metropolitan Chhatra Shakti unit. According to a letter issued by RU Shibir unit on 31 July, Shibir's monthly secretariat meeting in February 2025 decided to suspend Ammar's "Sathi" membership over allegations of moral misconduct, neglect of basic religious duties, freely mixing with women, illegal financial transactions and involvement in activities contrary to the organisation's aims and objectives. The letter said the September 2025 monthly secretariat meeting later decided to cancel his "Sathi" membership after he failed to adequately respond to the allegations. The letter also expressed concern that Ammar's activities and alleged involvement in "criminal activities" could create instability on campus. It said his "provocative activities" could also push the university towards conflict. Signed by Shibir's RU unit President Mujahid Faisal, the letter instructed Shibir leaders to stop communicating with Ammar. It also instructed activists to avoid Ammar in their online and offline activities and refrain from making any negative comments or reactions about him. It also urged elected Rucsu office-bearers not to maintain organisational ties with Ammar and asked Shibir activists at all levels to sever contact with him. Ahmed Munshi, sports secretary of the unit's 2025 committee, and two other leaders of its current committee confirmed the authenticity of the letter to The Business Standard today (30 September). A Shibir leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, said an investigation committee had been formed to look into various allegations against Ammar, including the theft of laptops from a city corporation building, trading in positions in the metropolitan Chhatra Shakti unit and financial irregularities. Asked about Ammar's political background, the leader said Ammar had originally been a "Sathi" of Shibir's Tamirul Millat Madrasah unit and worked with Alternative Literature - a cultural organisation at Rajshahi University. The leader claimed that the organisation was primarily run by Shibir members and that Ammar had been formally involved with Shibir until after the July Uprising in 2024. Another Shibir leader, also speaking on condition of anonymity, said the organisation initially suspended Ammar's membership under its rules and sought his response to the allegations. The decision to cancel his membership was taken after he failed to adequately respond, the leader said. The latest letter was issued after further alleged irregularities were observed and amid concerns over Ammar's conduct, the leader added. Previously, Ammar has repeatedly denied having any affiliation with Shibir. He was elected Rucsu general secretary from the "Anti-Dominance Unity" panel, which was widely discussed as a "dummy panel" of Shibir during the 2025 Rucsu election. He later drew controversy over several campus incidents, including multiple mob incidents, alleged irregularities in financial transactions involving Rucsu funds and incidents in which students were beaten. During that time, Shibir's RU unit said at a press conference that it would not take responsibility for Ammar. This reporter made several attempts to contact Ammar for comment, but received no response. title: BMW F 450 R: Four variants, prices and differences from the GS - motorcycles.news
content:
After the F 450 GS adventure tourer, BMW Motorrad’s new twin-cylinder engine gets its second home. The F 450 R has been developed as a standalone naked bike, but uses the GS’s engine, frame and swingarm as its basis. It is part of the new arrivals for the 2027 model year and, according to BMW, is not only aimed at riders with an A2 licence. The manufacturer also has returning riders and experienced motorcyclists in mind who are looking for a light bike for town and country roads. The price stands out in particular: at 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars), the base model undercuts the Aprilia Tuono 457. In Germany, the BMW F 450 R costs between 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars) and 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). The price difference comes down to the equipment and paintwork of the four variants. The base model is only available in Cosmic Black. Even this version comes with three riding modes, ABS Pro, traction control, a 6.5-inch TFT display and heated grips. What it lacks is the shift assistant. The F 450 R Exclusive is also black and costs 6,770 euros (around 7,599 US dollars). For an extra 280 euros, it adds Shift Assistant Pro and the so-called sport suspension, with a fork adjustable for rebound and compression damping. Anyone who wants a different colour has to go for the F 450 R M Sport. It costs 6,920 euros (around 7,768 US dollars) and is painted in Snaefell White / M Motorsport. This includes a white frame and rim stickers in the M colours. Alongside Shift Assistant Pro and sport suspension, Riding Modes Pro is also standard here. The fourth variant is the M Sport with Innovation Package for 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). It additionally comes with the Easy Ride Clutch. For comparison: the Aprilia Tuono 457 starts at 6,700 euros (around 7,521 US dollars). The most expensive F 450 R costs as much as the F 450 GS in its basic version. In the UK, the F 450 R is available from 6,395 pounds (around 7,521 euros / 8,442 US dollars). There are no plans for the USA yet, however. A BMW spokesperson said: “There are no current plans to bring the 2027 F 450 R to the US. The F 450 R may be introduced to the U.S. at a later date.” The F 450 R uses the liquid-cooled 420 cc parallel twin from the F 450 GS. It produces 48 hp (35 kW) at 8,750 rpm and delivers 43 Nm (32 lb-ft) at 6,750 rpm. For the naked bike, BMW has retuned the engine for road use. This does not change the performance figures. According to BMW, 80 per cent of maximum torque is already available at 3,000 rpm. So the engine does not have to be revved hard all the time to make brisk progress. The key data in detail: bore is 72 mm and stroke 51.6 mm. Two overhead camshafts operate four valves per cylinder via lightweight finger followers. The intake valves have a head diameter of 29 mm, the exhaust valves 24.3 mm. The compression ratio is 13:1. Port fuel injection with the BMS-Z engine management system prepares the mixture. The throttle is electronic: a sensor on the twistgrip reports the rider’s input to the engine management, which then opens the 38 mm throttle bodies. One special feature is the crankshaft. Its crankpins are offset by 135 degrees, which BMW says is unique on the motorcycle market. This results in an uneven firing interval and a distinctive sound. A balancer shaft in front of the crankshaft counters vibrations. To save weight, the clutch and transmission covers are made of magnesium. The stainless steel silencer sits under the engine and contains two catalytic converters. According to BMW, this solution saves around two kilograms. It is also meant to offer more lean angle and reduce the risk of the passenger or luggage being burned by a hot exhaust. BMW quotes fuel consumption of 3.8 litres per 100 kilometres according to the WMTC standard. With the 14-litre tank, this gives a theoretical range of up to 368 kilometres. The engine meets the Euro 5+ emissions standard and runs on premium unleaded. The F 450 R is said to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 5.7 seconds, with a top speed of 169 km/h. A six-speed gearbox transmits power to an X-ring chain on the left-hand side. Servicing is due every 10,000 kilometres. The Easy Ride Clutch is a centrifugal clutch that engages and disengages automatically depending on engine speed. To pull away, you simply open the throttle; when stopping, the clutch disengages by itself. A centrifugal clutch uses the outward force that builds as engine speed rises to close the clutch. Unlike many conventional systems, the BMW’s clutch stays closed on the overrun. Engine braking therefore works until just before the bike comes to a standstill. The clutch only opens once the engine reaches idle speed. This is meant to make it practically impossible to stall the engine. The clutch lever still remains on the handlebar. Anyone who prefers to modulate it themselves when manoeuvring or on twisty roads can use the clutch conventionally at any time. From the factory, the Easy Ride Clutch is only available on the M Sport as part of the Innovation Package. On the other variants, it can be retrofitted as Original BMW Motorrad Accessories. It adds one kilogram to the weight. Only in combination with Shift Assistant Pro can the F 450 R be ridden entirely without touching the clutch. The shift assistant allows clutchless upshifts and downshifts and therefore almost no interruption in drive. According to BMW, this also significantly reduces the head nodding of rider and passenger when changing gear. The shift assistant is standard on the Exclusive and M Sport and can be retrofitted to the base model. For track riding, the shift pattern can also be reversed with little effort. The F 450 R adopts the steel frame and aluminium swingarm of the F 450 GS, but its geometry, suspension, wheels and ergonomics are designed entirely for the road. Instead of an adventure look, the focus is on short distances and quick turn-in. Marc Weber, Lead Engineer Complete Vehicle for the F 450 R, puts it this way: “With the BMW F 450 R, we have consistently transferred the technical basis of the F 450 GS into a standalone BMW naked bike.” Chassis geometry, seating position and the entire package were retailored to the demands of the road. The trellis frame is made from welded steel tubes and forged parts, with the engine integrated as a load-bearing element. The wheelbase is 1,405 mm, the steering head angle 23.4 degrees and the trail 110 mm. At the front, a KYB upside-down fork with 43 mm inner tubes, gold-coloured stanchions and a forged aluminium triple clamp does the work. At the rear, a hollow-cast aluminium double-sided swingarm guides the wheel, combined with a directly mounted KYB shock absorber that is adjustable for preload and rebound. Suspension travel is 140 mm at both ends. The F 450 R rolls on 17-inch cast aluminium wheels with 110/70-17 tyres at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear. BMW fits the Eurogrip Protorq Extreme as standard. At the front, a floating 310 mm disc is gripped by a radially mounted Brembo four-piston monobloc caliper. At the rear sits a 240 mm disc with a single-piston floating caliper from ByBre. When it comes to weight, the F 450 R hits a limit set by the A2 regulations. They allow a maximum of 35 kW and a power-to-weight ratio of no more than 0.2 kW per kilogram. A full-power A2 motorcycle must therefore weigh at least 175 kilograms. That is exactly where the F 450 R sits at 175 kg (386 lbs) ready to ride, or 176 kg (388 lbs) with the Easy Ride Clutch. The Aprilia Tuono 457 achieves the same figures, but takes the opposite approach: its frame is aluminium and its swingarm steel. The BMW’s permissible total weight is 355 kg (783 lbs). All variants come as standard with the Rain, Road and Dynamic riding modes as well as ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control, Dynamic Traction Control and engine drag torque control. Added to this are a 6.5-inch TFT display, LED lighting, a USB-C socket and three-stage heated grips. The riding modes change throttle response and the control systems. Rain is intended for wet roads, with soft throttle response and a focus on stability. Road is designed for dry roads and a balanced set-up. In Dynamic, traction control, wheelie detection and engine drag torque control intervene later. Engine drag torque control prevents the rear wheel from locking when closing the throttle abruptly or downshifting. ABS Pro also works when leaned over and is meant to prevent the bike from standing up during panic braking in corners. Dynamic Brake Control detects when the rider accidentally opens the throttle during hard braking and keeps the throttle valves closed. The dynamic brake light warns following traffic of hard braking in two stages. Riding Modes Pro adds the Dynamic Pro mode, in which throttle response, ABS and traction control can be adjusted individually. The package is standard on the M Sport variants and available as an accessory for the base and Exclusive models. On the M Sport variants, the display then shows three additional Sport Screens with information on traction control, braking force and lean angle, as well as a lap timer. The TFT is operated via the Multi-Controller on the left handlebar end. Smartphone and helmet communication system can be paired via Bluetooth for phone calls or music, with no app required. Depending on the market, the free BMW Motorrad Connected app also shows arrow navigation on the display. Anyone wanting map navigation needs the navigation preparation available as an accessory, together with the ConnectedRide Navigator or ConnectedRide Smartphone Cradle. Visually, the F 450 R takes its cue from the S 1000 R with the “tail up, nose down” principle: the front sits low and the tail is raised high. The side panels form a stylised R, and the LED headlight features the bracket-shaped daytime running light of BMW’s naked bikes. Alexander Buckan, Head of Design at BMW Motorrad, says: “With its striking side panel and the naked-bike-typical flyline following the tail up – nose down principle, the BMW F 450 R unmistakably yet subtly quotes the design DNA of the S 1000 R without copying it one-to-one.” For the seating position, BMW relies on a high, 76 cm wide aluminium handlebar placed close to the rider. The two-piece standard seat is 790 mm high, and the inside leg curve measures 1,770 mm. A low accessory seat lowers the height to 775 mm, while a high sport seat raises it to 810 mm. Brake and clutch levers are adjustable as standard. The gear lever, footbrake lever and side stand are made of forged aluminium, and the passenger footrest brackets are bolted to the rear frame. Overall, the F 450 R is 2,002 mm long and 825 mm wide across the handlebar ends. BMW is offering a dedicated accessories range for the F 450 R from launch. According to BMW, deliveries of the naked bike are expected to start in June 2027. For everyday use and short trips, there are soft cases with 16.5 litres of capacity each including holders, a 5 to 8 litre tank bag that attaches directly to the fuel filler cap without straps, plus luggage rolls and tail bags in several sizes. A gold aluminium handlebar and black bar-end mirrors add visual accents. For protection, BMW offers engine protection bars, a radiator guard, hand guards, axle and engine protectors and M lever protectors. Depending on the variant, the Easy Ride Clutch, Shift Assistant Pro and Riding Modes Pro can also be retrofitted as accessories. In Germany, the BMW F 450 R costs from 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars). The Exclusive is priced at 6,770 euros, the M Sport at 6,920 euros and the M Sport with Innovation Package at 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). According to BMW, the F 450 R is expected to be available in Germany from June 2027. There are currently no plans for the USA. Yes, with 48 hp (35 kW) the F 450 R is designed for the European A2 licence category. No restriction is needed, as it does not exceed the permitted maximum output from the factory. The BMW F 450 R weighs 175 kg (386 lbs) ready to ride. With the optional Easy Ride Clutch, it weighs 176 kg (388 lbs). The F 450 R’s standard seat is 790 mm high. Accessory seats can lower it to 775 mm or raise it to 810 mm. ➜ This article is part of our comprehensive overview: New Motorcycles 2027: All Models, Releases and Highlights at a Glance. title: Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Jan Hatzius Joins CNBC to Discuss His Outlook for the US Economy - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Jan Hatzius joined CNBC to discuss his projections for near-term Fed policy following recent inflation and employment data. He anticipates a December rate hike, though he notes ongoing soft inflation readings could change that view. Let's bring in Jan Hatzius this morning at Post Nine. Goldman's chief economist get his first take on this report and sort of the week that we've had. Jan, good to have you back. It's good to be here. So we had we had Core PC and we had Williams Jefferson Bowman, and now this some of this stuff's kind of going your way in terms of your house view. Yes, in the sense that we don't need a lot of hikes from here. Yes, and we did push back the next move and final move in our forecast from the Fed from October to December on the heels of the PCE numbers. But all the events that you spoke about-the Williams speech, the Jefferson speech, and today's employment numbers-I think push in that same direction, that it's not we don't need a lot of monetary tightening here, and I think markets are discounting still three hikes, and I would say that's not necessary. I think December they've signaled one clearly. It was a reasonably clear baseline, so I think that is what they expect to do. And if we get no major news, it still would be my best guess. But it's certainly very possible that if we continue to see friendlier news, that they decide you can forego that, and then it would be a one-and-done hike. I don't think that's what they intended to deliver, but it all depends on the data, of course. Right. I mean, one and dones are not common, but they're not unprecedented. That's right. It's possible, but it's usually not what a central bank sets out to do because 25 basis points is just a very small number. Why would you go through the basically trouble of signaling it and and and working up to it, and then delivering it, but it's always going to be data dependent. Ongoing soft inflation numbers, in particular. So there's one CPI between now and the October meeting. That's going to be a really key data release, probably more important than the employment numbers. And you know, we think it's going to look reasonably friendly, sort of 0.2 percent, maybe a little bit above. That would certainly be consistent with not going in October. But if you continue to see 0.2 type of numbers, maybe December does not result in a hike. It seems part, Jan, of the market's over anticipation of further rate hikes beyond what you're looking for was somewhat related to this sort of momentum in the storyline about neutral rate. Maybe is higher. Maybe war signaled that 4% to four and a quarter, which would be one more hike. Maybe that's closer to what they think of as neutral. But also that financial conditions somehow need to tighten further. I was taken by the financial conditions indexes that you guys maintain, and when you eliminate equities from it, it actually was back toward like early 2025 tight levels. That's right. If you eliminate the the major driver of easing, which has been equities, because we've seen such a strong performance, then you do see significant tightening because, in particular, long-term interest rates have have risen quite significantly at this point. If you look at the whole thing, and I think you should probably include equities, although the weight is always going to be a subject of debate, I would say financial conditions are maybe a very small headwind to growth at these levels, but at this point, it's still not not really major. To me, if I look at the growth pace of the economy, we seem to be growing at basically a trend rate. The labor market looks stable. You can find some indicators like the U6 rate, for example, that have shown, you know, tightening labor market and improving labor market or continuing claims. You can look at some indicators like the Conference Board's measure of job availability that would say the labor market is loosening. If I take an average, it's approximately stable. So if inflation's not that pressing, you guys have written a lot about say hyperscaler issuance and just the competition, right, for capital, does that keep the long end elevated or something else? I do think the long end is more complicated. At the short end, I would say the market's pricing in too many hikes, so more likely than not, rates can come down. At the long end, that has some influence as well. What happens to inflation? What happens to the expected level of the funds rate, but then you have the supply issues, and those do point towards higher rates. So for that reason, we have less conviction. We also have long rates come down somewhat, but we have less conviction there than at the shorter end. So you're still looking at back to target on inflation by December 27? Not quite. We have it at 2.2 percent, pretty close. Essentially, there. Yeah. And at this point, you don't think any holds or any moves where they do not hike that doesn't add pressure to the long end. Where are we on that? Well, I think if they don't hike and the data supports the idea that it's not necessary to hike, then I don't. Think that would add pressure. We can see pressure if we had some unfriendly inflation release releases, and then they decided to basically defy market expectations for for a hike. Then you could see that kind of upward pressure. But that's not really our forecast. Is eurozone CPI today like a cautionary tale of what we might be in for next couple months. I mean, headline certainly is picking up there. The core numbers have generally been okay. I mean, we're at two and a half percent for core HICP. It's only risen, you know, relatively modestly, despite the fact that Europe is much more vulnerable to the energy situation because it's the gas issue in addition to the oil issue, but I would still say they can deliver, you know, maybe maybe one, you know, one more. But I wouldn't really expect a lot of tightening. Yeah, the ECB, the ECB. Sorry. The also because you know there are some signs of tightening in financial conditions, we did have quite a lot of turmoil in the sovereign bond market in Europe over the over the past week. So the ECB needs to tread carefully and look at all of the different drivers of policy before making any any significant moves. Yeah, I mean you saw a hotter than expected Tokyo CPI number two. To your point, so whether it's here in the U.S. or whether it's looking at the picture globally, does a resolution to the war in Iran actually change this entire conversation more quickly than anticipated? I mean, from a monetary policy perspective, I would have said if you'd asked me a year ago, when you know there's news about energy supply that cuts in both directions because it you know you resolve the situation in Iran that's a that's a boost to growth but it also helps inflation. I think that's become more clearly a sort of dovish development because markets have focused and policymakers have focused so much on the first round inflation effects, so that if you were to resolve it, it would probably help our forecast for fewer hikes than what markets are pricing. Finally, have you made any adjustments to AI impact on labor markets or productivity gains next year? Things like that, we have not really. I mean, our expectation continues to be that we'll see a substantial impact, but that it's you know going to be more spread over a longer period of time, perhaps than what what what others are saying. So we had this one and a half percentage point boost to long term growth from from AI before offsets from things like demographics and redirection of capital spending. We still have that in our numbers. I would say the news in terms of AI capabilities has been, you know, if anything, even stronger than what we've built into our numbers. But we haven't made any any formal changes at this point? We'll watch for that. Interesting. The saga continues. Jan, thank you. Good to see you. Thank you, Jan Hatzius.
